what_it_does: 3D Gaussian Splatting is a technique for representing and rendering a scene in 3D: rather than a mesh of triangles, the scene is described by millions of small fuzzy blobs (Gaussians), each with a position, shape, color, and opacity. SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) is the problem a robot or camera-equipped device faces when it must build a 3D map of a new environment while simultaneously tracking its own position within that map in real time. Combining these two — using 3D Gaussians as the map representation and updating them continuously as new camera frames arrive — requires training the Gaussian model incrementally at video speed (over 30 frames per second) on a low-power edge device, which existing hardware cannot do. REACT3D addresses this with two algorithmic shortcuts: it predicts which Gaussians are well-converged and skips retraining them, and it folds the error-computation step into the rendering step so intermediate results do not need to be stored. It also adds a specialized memory structure called a Content Addressable Memory (CAM) based dual-index buffer that quickly maps between scattered Gaussian blob identifiers and their gradient accumulation slots, solving the irregular memory access problem that arises when many pixels map to overlapping Gaussians.
